name: Job-shop scheduling ta48
description: Schedule 30 jobs on 20 machines (job-shop benchmark instance ta48). Every job is a sequence of 20 operations, one on each machine, that must run in the given order; an operation occupies its machine for its whole duration without interruption, and a machine processes one operation at a time. Minimise the makespan, the time at which the last operation ends.

Demirkol, Mehta and Uzsoy (1998), Benchmarks for shop scheduling problems: defines the 80 DMU job-shop instances (rcmax and cscmax subfamilies); benchmark paper, not primary evidence.
Taillard (1993), Benchmarks for basic scheduling problems: defines the Taillard (ta) job-shop instances; benchmark paper, not primary evidence.
Storer, Wu and Vaccari (1992), New Search Spaces for Sequencing Problems with Application to Job Shop Scheduling: origin of the SWV instances.
van Hoorn (2018), The Current state of bounds on benchmark instances of the job-shop scheduling problem: compiled bounds as of 2017.

Heinz, Hanzalek and Vilim (2024), Reinforcement Learning for Search Tree Size Minimization in Constraint Programming: New Results on Scheduling Benchmarks; Shylo's page credits most older lower bounds to it (code RL2024), but the task's lower bound is the larger OptalCP value of the ScheduleOpt table for almost every instance.

execution.interface: solve(inst) -> starts, a list of n_jobs lists of non-negative integers: starts[j][k] is the start time of operation k of job j. inst has name, n_jobs, n_machines and jobs[j] = list of (machine, duration) pairs in processing order, machines numbered from 0. Operation k + 1 of a job may not start before operation k has ended, and two operations on one machine may not overlap (one may start at the moment the other ends). Score: the makespan, minimized.

science_relevance.reason: The two papers have the job-shop scheduling problem itself as their main objective (its complexity and the state of its solution methods), and the evaluator scores exactly the makespan of a feasible schedule of the pinned instance; the record papers in the overrides add the work that holds the best known makespan.
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Find machine sequences, as start times, of minimum makespan for the open job-shop benchmark instance ta48.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Job-shop scheduling is the canonical model of machine scheduling in manufacturing and is NP-hard in the strong sense; the instances of this family are still open, meaning the best known makespan is above the best proven lower bound, so a shorter schedule is a new best known upper bound.
